html:
SMTO-SKL-0021 — SMTO didn't recognize that time zone

GUID: 0619fc94-d2bb-5f17-bade-3c99cc851b3e
Slug: google-calendar-invalid-timezone
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • The time zone in this calendar request isn't one SMTO recognizes, so it couldn't work out the times. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask again and give the time zone by a major city or region, for example "New York time" or "Europe/London", not an abbreviation like "PST". City-based time zone names are the standard ones SMTO can look up, and they handle daylight saving correctly.
  2. If you're editing an existing event and don't mean to change its time zone, leave the time zone out of your request. SMTO then keeps the event's current time zone instead of trying a new one.
  3. If a common city time zone like "America/New_York" is also refused, tell the person who manages SMTO. That means the computer running SMTO is missing its time zone data, which you can't fix from the conversation.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request and the event shows the time in the time zone you named.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time zone you used, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • zoneinfo.ZoneInfo could not resolve the supplied Calendar timezone because the key is unknown, has an invalid value or is not a string.

What this means

  • ZoneInfo cannot resolve the supplied timezone because it is unknown or has an invalid value/type. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • ZoneInfo cannot resolve the supplied timezone because it is unknown or has an invalid value/type.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the exact zone name and installed timezone data.

How to fix it

  • Pass an IANA timezone key such as America/Los_Angeles and keep the event's existing timeZone when editing. If valid IANA keys also fail, the Server's Python runtime is missing tz data; install the system tz database or the tzdata Python package.
  • Use an explicit IANA timezone such as America/Los_Angeles, preserving the event timezone when editing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an explicit IANA timezone such as America/Los_Angeles, preserving the event timezone when editing.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended IANA timezone resolves and event offsets remain consistent.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
